# Sergeant SOP This is the list of procedures, responsibilities, and duties of the [color=#ba292c][bold]Sergeant[/bold][/color] of this station.
For the purposes of Alert Escalation: Treat higher alerts as if they are still on the previous alert level. (Yellow Alert is Blue Alert if it was Blue Alert prior.) Furthermore, treat Delta, Gamma, Epsilon, and Violet Alert as Red Alert.
The Sergeant is a senior role to all other [bold][color=#ba292c]Security[/color][/bold] personnel except the [bold][color=#ba292c]Warden[/color][/bold] and the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Head of Security[/bold][/color].
When selecting an Acting HoS or Acting Warden, the Sergeant should be considered above all other Security personnel. Should either become incapacitated, the Sergeant should assume the respective role as soon as is convenient for the situation. The Sergeant as an Acting HoS or Acting Warden will fully assume the associated responsibilities, including ensuring the efficacy of the department as a whole instead of solely focusing on training.
The Sergeant shares all responsibilities of Security personnel but is to prioritize training, directing, advising, and leading officers and cadets. To this end, the [textlink="Security Officer SOP" link="OfficerCadetSOP"] should be consulted for escalation procedures in regards to alert level. Failure to perform these priorities or to act as a role model is grounds for demotion.
The Sergeant is permitted to carry their shift-start equipment, but they should follow escalation procedures and refrain from using lethals unless required to [italic]beyond a reasonable doubt[/italic].
## Green Alert 1. The Sergeant is expected to instruct [color=#ba292c][bold]Security Cadets[/bold][/color] on how to perform their duties and to guide other Security personnel should they ask for help. [bold]Cadets are to be prioritized first[/bold], but should the cadet decline help, the Sergeant does not need to focus their attention on them. The Sergeant should be open-minded to all available methods when teaching staff, even if it may not be the most familiar to the Sergeant.
2. The Sergeant is expected to fulfill the duties of other Security personnel [bold]if and only if[/bold] there are no Security Cadets needing to be instructed. In addition, when assuming other duties, the Sergeant is expected to follow the same SOP as the role they will perform. Follow the guidelines of the [textlink="Security Officer SOP" link="OfficerCadetSOP"] according to the alert level when conducting arrests (respecting permitted equipment as outlined below).
3. The Sergeant is expected to have a comprehensive understanding of the SOP and duties of each departmental role and may be consulted at any time regarding proper procedure. Additionally, the Sergeant must ensure their department is following SOP and is expected to remind staff and/or the department head to do so. The [color=#ba292c][bold]Sergeant[/bold][/color] must comply with all LEGAL orders from the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Head of Security[/bold][/color] and the [bold][color=#ba292c]Warden[/color][/bold]. In situations where either is in violation of spacelaw, the Sergeant is expected to work with the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Captain[/bold][/color] and the [color=#1b67a5][bold]Nanotrasen Representative[/bold][/color] to appropriately handle the breach of conduct.
4. The Sergeant should be clearly distinguishable from other staff of their department, meaning that they ought to wear the appropriately designated clothing for their role. Consequently, the Sergeant should not give to other personnel any Nanotrasen property assigned to them except for instructional use or in case of station-threatening emergency.
5. The Sergeant is permitted to acquire surplus equipment and apparel of their department explicitly for training or ceremonial purposes (while respecting [color=#388c34]Green Alert[/color] Guideline 9 if it is in effect).
6. The Sergeant may ask certain departmental personnel to vacate equipment for the sake of training. However, this request may be refused if there is an urgent need or if it would be unwise to vacate at that moment. Unreasonable refusal to vacate is grounds for disciplinary action should the department head find it necessary.
7. The Sergeant is permitted to carry all standard security items appropriate to an officer, their trench whistle, and their signature Nanotrasen-approved ceremonial weapon. While permitted to carry their unique ceremonial weapon, use should be for ceremony and training except if non-lethal.
8. In the absence of the Warden, the Sergeant may conduct sentencing. These sentences may be overruled by the Warden or the Head of Security if either disagrees.
9. The Sergeant is not permitted to collect equipment from the Armory to carry on their person.
10. The Sergeant is not permitted to use their whistle outside of training and ceremony.
## Blue Alert 1. All guidelines except 9 and 10 carry over from [color=#388c34]Green Alert[/color]. Additionally, the ceremonial weapon may be used lethally if needed.
2. The Sergeant is allowed to use their whistle as necessary.
3. The Sergeant should prioritize leading and directing hands-on Security operations to allow the Head of Security and the Warden to maintain command and overwatch over the Security department as a whole.
## Red Alert 1. All guidelines carry over from [color=#1b67a5]Blue Alert[/color].
2. All guidelines except 9 and 10 carry over from [color=#388c34]Green Alert[/color].
3. The Sergeant may wear a hardsuit if necessary.
